source_name: MNB 19/2025. (VI.26.) ATM-telepítési rendelet + settlement/bank allocation lists
why_relevant: The regulation names, settlement by settlement, which bank must install an ATM (>=1000 inhabitants by 2025-12-31, >=500 by 2026-12-31), plus mandatory inter-bank delegation contracts (min. 5 years, signed by 2025-07-31) and escalating fines to HUF 150m. This creates a dated, bank-attributed ATM demand pipeline — the strongest public driver of vendor orders in HU.

source_name: MNB tájékoztató a nyilvánosságra hozatal szabályozásáról (disclosure regulation guidance notes)
why_relevant: MNB's own explanatory note on the disclosure regime — maps which institutions owe which Pillar 3 templates and on what schedule, which tells the collection pipeline what to expect from each bank and when.

source_name: MNB licensing guidance library for payment institutions and EMIs
why_relevant: Defines the legal categories, capital and reporting obligations that determine what each actor in this cell must disclose and to whom. Essential for interpreting why one PSP files a full audited beszámoló while another (a passported branch) files almost nothing locally.

source_name: BÉT / KIB newkibdata – Erste Bank Hungary Pillar 3 (Kockázati Jelentés) PDFs
why_relevant: Erste Bank Hungary is a bond issuer on BÉT, so its Pillar 3 / risk reports are also filed into the exchange's issuer-disclosure store (newkibdata). This is a second, more machine-friendly copy of documents that are awkward to reach on the bank site.

source_name: OPUS GLOBAL Nyrt. – konszolidált éves jelentés (BÉT-listed holding with financial arms)
why_relevant: Large BÉT-listed holding (top-5 capitalisation) whose consolidated annual reports document its financial-sector participations, ratings (Scope BB/stable) and funding — the practical entry point to the Opus/4iG-adjacent financial arms named in this cell.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Bankszövetségi Krónikák a digitális átállás korszakában (Kovács Levente)
why_relevant: Book-length association chronicle by the Secretary General covering the digital-transition era; contains a 2024 member-institution list and a longitudinal account of sector policy, consolidation and digitalisation milestones — a ready-made historical baseline for the HU banking narrative.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — bank/insurer ranking series ('bankok és biztosítók rangsora')
why_relevant: Recurring (roughly annual, early June, keyed to the 31 May statutory annual-account filing deadline) structured league table built from Hungarian banks' and insurers' filed annual accounts. This is one of the few places where balance-sheet-total and profit rankings across ALL Hungarian banks — including small/foreign-owned subsidiaries — appear in one comparable table.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Aktualitások / press releases (results, dividend, financial services)
why_relevant: Posta's press releases carry headline results ahead of the full report (e.g. 2024 after-tax profit ~HUF 5.2bn, first dividend since 2009, HUF 1,355bn government-securities stock distributed). Earliest public earnings signal for the postal payments arm.

source_name: Bankmonitor – fintech/bank market commentary
why_relevant: Analyses pricing and T&C changes at Revolut/Wise-type providers as they localise into Hungary — a proxy disclosure channel where the issuers publish only terms documents, no local press releases.

source_name: CIB Bank Zrt. – IFRS éves beszámolók (document/publications store)
why_relevant: Intesa Sanpaolo's Hungarian subsidiary publishes its separate and consolidated IFRS accounts as PDFs under year/announcement-structured document paths rather than a conventional IR page; this is the only entity-level CIB P&L.

source_name: BKR Üzletszabályzat és Díjszabályzat (GIRO clearing rulebook and tariff schedule)
why_relevant: The rulebook and the annual tariff schedule are the only public statement of BKR/GIROInstant per-transaction pricing and participant obligations — the scheme economics that the annual report only aggregates. Versioned yearly, so a time series of tariffs is buildable.

source_name: MBH Bank – Alaptájékoztató / kibocsátási program (HUF 500bn base prospectus)
why_relevant: Base prospectuses are the single richest structured description of a Hungarian bank: business model, risk factors, group structure, funding, litigation, and segment financials — all in one MNB-approved document, refreshed annually.

source_name: Revolut Bank UAB Magyarországi Fióktelepe – company record and Revolut HU announcements
why_relevant: Revolut completed the regulatory steps for a Hungarian branch in Oct 2025 and was entered in the MNB register as 'Revolut Bank UAB Magyarországi Fióktelepe'; in March 2026 it announced migration of Hungarian users to the local branch with domestic HUF IBANs. It reports customer milestones (2 million Hungarian retail customers reached July 2025) via press announcements rather than local IR. Branch accounts and registry data are the only structured local disclosure.

source_name: Privátbankár.hu — Hungarian coverage of foreign parents' Hungarian results
why_relevant: Second independent Hungarian outlet tracking parent-group disclosures about Hungarian levies and subsidiary results; useful for triangulating Portfolio.hu and for catching stories Portfolio paywalls.

source_name: UniCredit Fixed Income & ESG presentation (quarterly)
why_relevant: A second, deeper quarterly deck aimed at debt investors — typically carries more granular per-country funding, asset-quality and balance-sheet detail for CEE entities than the equity results deck, including Hungary.

source_name: Világgazdaság (vg.hu) – payments and fintech reporting
why_relevant: Consistently first to report Revolut Hungary branch/IBAN milestones and PSP funding rounds, often quoting company statements verbatim. A practical proxy channel for issuers (Revolut, Wise) that publish no Hungarian-language IR material.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide press releases on Hungarian bank ATM outsourcing
why_relevant: Named deal disclosure: 10-year ATM outsourcing extension with Budapest Bank covering its ~145-ATM network. Exactly the vendor-side trace of a Hungarian bank technology decision that never appears on a procurement portal.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal – Hungarian business register country page
why_relevant: Neutral English-language description of what the Hungarian company register contains, who operates it, what is free vs. paid, and BRIS interconnection — useful for validating access assumptions and for non-Hungarian-speaking analysts on the team.

source_name: Forbes.hu – business/fintech coverage
why_relevant: Runs exclusive funding-round scoops on Hungarian payment fintechs (e.g. a EUR 10m round disclosed exclusively) and periodic landscape pieces naming the players worth tracking — a productive snowball surface for actor discovery.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo IR press-release archive — Hungary-tagged releases
why_relevant: Demonstrates that Intesa's IR press-release archive is topically indexed and reaches back over a decade, including Hungary-specific announcements (capital injections, restructurings, CIB milestones). Good for building the historical event timeline behind CIB Bank.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — Results & Reports (quarterly/semi-annual PDFs)
why_relevant: RBI reports Hungary as a named country segment inside Central Europe, with NII, net commission income (explicitly broken out for clearing/settlement/payment services and FX — directly payments-relevant), loan volumes and risk costs. Highest-value payments KPI text in the whole cell.

source_name: Scope Ratings - MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank rating actions
why_relevant: MFB is a state development bank with thin English disclosure; the Scope release restates the statutory state guarantee, funding structure and sovereign linkage - disclosure-grade facts available nowhere else in English.

source_name: Telex.hu – economy desk (payments/licensing coverage)
why_relevant: Covers MNB licensing events for new entrants — e.g. Pay10 receiving an e-money licence and building its EU network from Budapest. Licence-grant news is the earliest signal that a new EMI will start filing Hungarian accounts.

source_name: Az én pénzem (azenpenzem.hu) – consumer-finance desk
why_relevant: Tracks new entrants to the Hungarian payment market from a consumer angle; catches smaller PSP/EMI launches that the business press ignores. Cheap breadth for the long tail of the cell.

entity_name: Cofidis Group / Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale
source_name: Cofidis Group / Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale — new parent of Magyar Cetelem Bank
why_relevant: OWNERSHIP CORRECTION for this cell: Magyar Cetelem Bank Zrt. is no longer a BNP Paribas Personal Finance subsidiary — Cofidis Group (Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale) completed its acquisition in October 2024. Forward-looking parent-IR coverage of Hungarian consumer credit must therefore track Crédit Mutuel / BFCM investor disclosures, not BNP Paribas.

source_name: Earnings-call transcript mirrors (Investing.com, Seeking Alpha, Yahoo Finance)
why_relevant: Q&A on parent earnings calls is where Hungary-specific colour is given — bank-levy quantification (e.g. EUR 189m charged in Hungary in Q2 2026 incl. EUR 121m full-year banking tax), interest-cap extension effects, retail loan momentum. These mirrors are the most searchable rendering of that dialogue.

entity_name: Erste Group annual report filed with Bucharest Stock Exchange
source_name: Erste Group annual report filed with Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB infocont)
why_relevant: Erste is dual-listed (Vienna, Prague, Bucharest); the BVB regulatory filing archive mirrors the full annual report as a stable, non-bot-defended PDF. Useful redundancy when erstegroup.com assets move, and a timestamped regulatory copy.

entity_name: Hungarian municipal 'kihelyezett ATM szolgáltatási szerződés' documents
source_name: Hungarian municipal 'kihelyezett ATM szolgáltatási szerződés' documents (e.g. Onga)
why_relevant: Municipalities publish the actual ATM placement/service contracts in their council agendas. A retrieved example names MBH Bank Nyrt. and lists Diebold Nixdorf Kft. as the bank's authorised ATM operating partner — a rare public document that directly links a systemic Hungarian bank to its ATM vendor.

source_name: KBC Group Quarterly Report (PDF series, wcmassets CDN)
why_relevant: The actual quarterly document containing Hungary segment figures: K&H net result, NII, loan and deposit volumes, cost/income, impairments, plus Hungarian regulatory shocks (extra-profit/windfall bank and insurance tax, mortgage interest-rate cap, modification losses). Directly quotable numeric series per quarter.

entity_name: KBC results distributed via GlobeNewswire / Ritzau newswire mirrors
source_name: KBC results distributed via GlobeNewswire / Ritzau newswire mirrors
why_relevant: Regulated-information newswires mirror the identical KBC quarterly report PDFs at publication minute. Useful as a redundancy/liveness channel when kbc.com assets rotate their CDN cache tokens, and gives a timestamped record of when the Hungary numbers became public.

source_name: MKVK Oktatási Központ (MKVKOK) - sector guidance 'Hitelintézetek beszámolójának elemzése'
why_relevant: Professional-training material explaining how Hungarian credit-institution statutory accounts are structured and audited. Methodology source: tells the collector what line items and audit judgements to expect in filed bank accounts, and the correct Hungarian terminology for parsing them.
